title: Section 26AH ITAA 1936 — bonuses on short-term life assurance policies
summary: Bonuses received under eligible life assurance policies are assessable within the 10-year eligible period — full amount in years 1-8, two-thirds in year 9, one-third in year 10. Eligible policy = life assurance policy with commencement of risk after 27 August 1982 (not a post-2002 funeral policy). Deemed receipt where bonuses are reinvested (unless surrender/maturity value increases); unit-value increases on unit-linked policies are deemed bonuses; death and illness benefits are excluded; a 25% premium increase restarts the eligible period. A 30% rebate applies under s 160AAB and CGT on surrender/maturity is disregarded to the extent s 26AH applies. Subsection coverage: operative 1,3,4,5,6,7,9,11,13 mapped to nodes; 2 (paid-up policy in lieu — deemed continuation) and 12 (sale/assignment — CGT disposal) noted as machinery; 6A (non-complying super fund) and 14 (pre-1983 transitional) out of scope for the standard investment-bond pattern.

nodes.label: You hold a life assurance policy and receive an amount under it as or by way of a bonus
nodes.body: Section 26AH taxes bonuses received under short-term life assurance policies ('eligible policies') within a 10-year eligible period. Amounts received after the 10th year are not assessable. A 30% rebate is available under s 160AAB.

rulings.title: Income tax: bonuses paid on certain life assurance policies — section 26AH — interpretation and operation

nodes.label: Is the policy an 'eligible policy'?
nodes.body: An eligible policy is a life assurance policy with a date of commencement of risk after 27 August 1982, other than a funeral policy (as defined in ITAA 1997) issued on or after 1 January 2003. If it is not an eligible policy, s 26AH does not apply at all.

nodes.label: Is the amount received as or by way of a bonus?
nodes.body: The charging provision (s 26AH(6)) catches amounts received during the eligible period as or by way of a bonus that would otherwise not be assessable. An amount received otherwise than as or by way of a bonus may be deemed a bonus under s 26AH(9) if the Commissioner opines it represents an accrued/declared/expected bonus.

nodes.label: Was the amount received during the eligible period (as modified by s 26AH(13) and s 26AH(14))?
nodes.body: The eligible period is generally 10 years from the date of commencement of risk (s 26AH(1)), but: (a) if premiums increase >25%, the period re-reckons from the premium increase year for receipts after that year and before the first subsequent eligible reckoning date (s 26AH(13)); (b) for policies with date of commencement of risk on or before 7 December 1983, the eligible period is 4 years with fractions of 100%/two-thirds/one-third in years 2-4 (s 26AH(14)).

nodes.label: Was the bonus actually paid to you, or reinvested/dealt with on your behalf?
nodes.body: A taxpayer is taken to have received an amount even if it is not actually paid but is reinvested or dealt with on their behalf or as directed (s 26AH(4)).

nodes.label: Did the reinvestment increase the amount expected on surrender or maturity?
nodes.body: Subsection (4) does not apply where the amount is reinvested so as to increase the amount that might reasonably be expected to be received on surrender or maturity (s 26AH(5)) — so bonuses merely credited and retained in the policy are not taxed during the policy's life.

nodes.label: Does an exclusion under s 26AH(7) or a Commissioner determination under s 26AH(8) apply?
nodes.body: Subsection (6) does not apply if: (a) the amount is in consequence of death/illness/disability of the insured; (aa) the policy is an RSA; (b) held by trustee of complying super fund/ADF/PST; (ba) life company liabilities discharged out of complying superannuation assets or segregated exempt assets; (c) (with carve-out) the amount is from forfeiture/surrender/termination due to serious financial difficulties. Also, the Commissioner may determine it unreasonable for s 26AH(6) to apply under s 26AH(8) having regard to premiums paid, amounts received, surrender value and other matters.

nodes.label: Calculate the assessable portion of the bonus
nodes.body: Full amount assessable if received in the first 8 years; two-thirds if received in the 9th year; one-third if received in the 10th year (s 26AH(6)). For pre-7 Dec 1983 policies (s 26AH(14)): full in first 2 years, two-thirds in 3rd year, one-third in 4th year. A 30% rebate may apply under s 160AAB if the policy was issued by a life assurance company (or specified state insurer/friendly society with varying statutory percentages) and the amount is an 'eligible 26AH amount'. Capital gains on a policy of insurance on a life may be disregarded under s 118-300 ITAA 1997 in the table-specified situations (items 3-7) — the disregard is not tied to the extent s 26AH applies.

rulings.title: Assessability of bonuses received upon termination of a life insurance policy

nodes.label: Did premiums increase by more than 25% in any assurance year (s 26AH(13))?
nodes.body: If the premiums payable in an assurance year (the 'premium increase year') exceed those of the immediately preceding year by more than 25%, the eligible period is reckoned from the date of commencement of that premium increase year for: (a) amounts received after that date and before the first subsequent eligible reckoning date (if any); and (b) sales/assignments after that date and before the first subsequent eligible reckoning date (s 26AH(13)(a)-(b)). This re-reckons the eligible period for those specific receipts only — it is not a general restart of a new 10-year clock.

rulings.title: Income tax: does section 26AH apply when investment options are 'switched' under an eligible policy?

nodes.label: Bonus is assessable (with the s 160AAB 30% rebate); CGT on the policy is disregarded to that extent
nodes.body: The assessable portion is included in assessable income of the year received (s 26AH(6)). The s 160AAB rebate reduces the tax payable on it. On surrender or maturity, capital gains are disregarded to the extent s 26AH applied (s 118-300 ITAA 1997).

nodes.label: Bonus is not assessable under s 26AH
nodes.body: No amount is included in assessable income under s 26AH — the bonus is not taxed (or, if received in consequence of death or illness, it retains its normal character).

nodes.label: Complete — the bonus is either assessable (with rebate) or not assessable under s 26AH
Did you receive an advance or loan from the assurer at nil or below-arm's-length interest?
nodes.body: An advance or loan from the assurer (or another person at the assurer's request/agreement) on which interest is not payable, or is payable below the arm's length rate, is deemed to be an amount to which paragraph 26AH(9)(a) applies (s 26AH(11)) — i.e. it is treated as a non-bonus amount that may then be deemed a bonus under s 26AH(9).

nodes.label: Did you receive a non-bonus amount that may represent an accrued/expected bonus?
nodes.body: Where, otherwise than as or by way of a bonus, a taxpayer receives an amount under an eligible policy and the Commissioner is of the opinion that it represents the whole or part of a bonus that has accrued/has been declared/can reasonably be expected to accrue, the amount is deemed to have been received as or by way of a bonus (s 26AH(9)). Section 26AH(10) prevents double taxation if the actual bonus is later received.

nodes.label: Was a paid-up life assurance policy issued in lieu of this eligible policy?
nodes.body: Where a paid-up life assurance policy is issued to a taxpayer in lieu of an eligible policy: (a) the paid-up policy is deemed to be a continuation of the eligible policy; and (b) no amount is taken under s 26AH(4) to have been reinvested in connection with the issue of the paid-up policy (s 26AH(2)).

nodes.label: Is the eligible policy held by the trustee of a non-complying superannuation fund?
nodes.body: If the amount is received during the eligible period in relation to an eligible policy held by the trustee of a non-complying superannuation fund: (a) s 26AH(6) does not apply; and (b) the amount is included in the fund's assessable income (s 26AH(6A)).

nodes.label: Was an actual bonus subsequently received after a s 26AH(9) opinion?
nodes.body: Where s 26AH(9) applied because the Commissioner formed an opinion that part of an amount represents a bonus, and the taxpayer later receives the actual bonus: (c) the operation of s 26AH(9) is unaffected; and (d) no part of the actual bonus is included in assessable income (s 26AH(10)). This prevents double taxation.

nodes.label: Did you sell or assign the policy (or rights under it) during the eligible period?
nodes.body: Where an eligible policy, or any right to receive benefits under it, is sold or assigned during the eligible period: (a) the consideration is deemed to be an amount to which s 26AH(9)(a) applies; and (b) s 26AH(9) and (10) apply as if 'is attributable to' replaced 'represents' (s 26AH(12)). The consideration is then assessed under the s 26AH(9) deemed-bonus mechanism.
